sections.h2: Who sets and collects property tax in Whitley County, Kentucky?
sections.html:
Two offices handle most of it. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) values every parcel, and the Whitley County Sheriff mails the bill and takes payment. The Whitley County Fiscal Court lists the Property Valuation office at (606) 549-6008 or 6009 and the sheriff at (606) 549-6006 or 6007, and the county offices sit in the courthouse at 200 Main Street in Williamsburg. The sheriff's website offers an online tax bill search.

If a bill goes unpaid, the County Clerk takes over after April 15. The clerk, not the sheriff, quotes payoff figures on delinquent parcels and runs the county's tax bill sale.

Whitley is a big, hilly county in the southeast corner of the state. It covers 445 square miles on the Cumberland Plateau, and elevations run from 723 to 2,220 feet. Williamsburg is the county seat, while Corbin is the largest city and sits partly in Knox and Laurel counties. Three school districts serve the county: Whitley County Schools, Williamsburg Independent and Corbin Independent. Your bill includes a school district rate, so the district your house sits in matters.

sections.h2: What do homes and owners look like in Whitley County?
sections.html:
Homes here cost far less than the Kentucky Bluegrass counties, and that shapes how much tax a typical seller owes. The Census Bureau's QuickFacts for 2020 to 2024 gives a median owner occupied home value of $131,800 and a median household income of $44,615. About 66.8 percent of households own their home.

  • Housing units: 15,904 as of July 2025.
  • Median gross rent: $798 a month.
  • Owners without a mortgage pay a median of $346 a month in costs, with a mortgage $1,156.
  • New home permits: 52 in 2025.
  • Persons in poverty: 25.5 percent.

The county's 2020 census count was 36,712, and the 2025 estimate is 37,297, growth of 1.6 percent.

sections.h2: What dates and penalties apply to a Whitley County tax bill?
sections.html:
The state sets one calendar for the whole commonwealth in KRS 134.015. A payment made by November 1 earns a 2 percent discount. From November 2 through December 31 you pay the face amount. A payment in January carries a 5 percent penalty, and after January 31 the penalty is 10 percent.

Tax follows the person who owned the house on January 1 of the assessment year, and the bill is that owner's personal debt. A seller who closes in spring still has to deal with the previous year's bill, which may already be a lien. The lien can stay on the parcel for 11 years under KRS 134.420, whoever owns it next.

  • Ask the sheriff whether the current year's bill is paid and in whose name it was issued.
  • Ask the County Clerk whether any earlier year was sold as a certificate of delinquency.
  • Have the title company confirm both before the closing date.

sections.h2: What happens to a Whitley County bill that stays unpaid?
sections.html:
On April 15 the sheriff hands every unpaid bill to the County Clerk, where it becomes a certificate of delinquency and a lien is recorded. Interest at 1 percent a month starts, and the clerk adds a commission of 10 percent. If the county attorney sends a notice, a 20 percent commission is added too. The Department of Revenue shows how fast this grows with a $1,000 bill.

What a $1,000 Kentucky bill costs as it moves through delinquency
StageTotal due
Face amount at the sheriff$1,000.00
Transferred to the clerk, with 10% penalty and sheriff add-ons$1,254.00
Paid within five business days of transfer$1,387.79
Paid after the first county attorney notice$1,611.30
Paid in June after advertising$1,659.90

Source: Kentucky Department of Revenue, The Collection Process for Property Tax Bills. The department's examples assume a 4 percent sheriff commission, so a county's real figures differ slightly.

The clerk then advertises the bills and schedules a sale between 90 and 135 days after the transfer. The Whitley County Clerk scheduled the sale of 2025 bills for September 17, 2026, at the courthouse, run as a lottery that limits each registered buyer to three bills. If a third party buys your certificate, you pay that buyer, and buyers can add fees.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Whitley County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with the PVA office, because Kentucky does not allow an appeal until you have talked to it. The assessment date is January 1, and notices go out in the spring. The tax roll then sits open for public inspection for 13 days starting the first Monday in May.

Hold your conference with the PVA or a deputy during that window. If you still disagree, file your appeal with the County Clerk by the close of business on the workday after the inspection period ends. The local board of assessment appeals meets 25 to 35 days later. It denies appeals that come without facts, so bring evidence:

  • Sale prices of similar houses nearby that closed recently.
  • Repair estimates or photos if the house is in worse shape than the record shows.
  • Your insurance policy or construction cost figures.

The PVA normally values homes by comparing them to recent sales, and every parcel must be inspected at least once in four years. The PVA can show you the list of sales it used for your parcel, so ask for it before you decide whether to appeal.

sections.h2: Who qualifies for the Whitley County homestead exemption?
sections.html:
A homeowner who is 65 or older, or totally disabled, can deduct a set dollar amount from assessed value. The deduction applies to the home where you live permanently, and a married couple gets one exemption even if both spouses are over 65. Apply to the PVA on Form 62A350. Once approved, the exemption continues each year while the original applicant still owns and lives in the home.

The exemption belongs to the owner, not to the house. If you sell, the buyer must file their own application if they qualify. The state resets the deduction amount every two years, so ask the PVA for the current figure instead of trusting an old number. Totally disabled veterans and owners with a permanent Social Security disability finding do not have to reapply each year.

sections.h2: What should a Whitley County seller check before closing?
sections.html:
Treat taxes as a payoff item, the same as a mortgage. The title company asks the sheriff and the County Clerk for balances, and anything owed comes out of your proceeds at the closing table. Surprises tend to come from older years, not the current bill.

  • Confirm the owner name on the bill matches the deed.
  • Check for omitted property bills if you added a garage, a mobile home or an outbuilding.
  • If the house is inherited, make sure the bill was not mailed to a person who has died.
  • Ask the clerk whether any certificate of delinquency has been sold to a private buyer.

A buyer who pays cash can usually settle these items within a week or two of agreeing on a price, because no lender has to review the payoff statements.

faqs.q: Where do I pay my Whitley County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay the Whitley County Sheriff. The sheriff's website has an online tax bill search, and the fiscal court lists the sheriff's office at (606) 549-6006 or 6007. After April 15 an unpaid bill moves to the County Clerk.

faqs.q: Does the Whitley County Sheriff accept late payments?
faqs.a: Yes, until April 15, with penalties. Kentucky adds 5 percent in January and 10 percent after January 31, as KRS 134.015 sets out. After April 15 the clerk collects, and 1 percent monthly interest and commissions apply.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Whitley County house that has unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Delinquent tax is paid from the sale proceeds at closing, and the title company gets payoff figures from the sheriff and the County Clerk. A lien stays on the parcel until it is paid, so the balance must be cleared before a clean transfer.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal my Whitley County assessment?
faqs.a: File with the County Clerk by the close of the workday after the roll inspection period ends. That period starts the first Monday in May and runs 13 days. You must first meet with the PVA.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Whitley County assessment?
faqs.a: Call the Property Valuation office at the courthouse, listed by the fiscal court at (606) 549-6008 or 6009. Questions about the bill amount or payment go to the sheriff instead, and delinquent bills go to the County Clerk.
